entries.title: A plan to get lifesaving food to malnourished kids was working -- until it wasn't
entries.snippet: Through an innovative program, parents in Senegal had easy access to a therapeutic food that's a boon for malnourished kids. Now there are shortages. Health specialists say U.S. aid cuts are to blame.

entries.title: 'Cool Ladies Club' is directed by 10 working-class women. They live up to the title
entries.snippet: They gave smartphones to 10 women from a working-class Indian community to make a documentary about their unseen and unheralded lives. The results are .... pretty cool.

entries.title: COMIC: How excessive heat kills and how to stay safe

entries.title: Pope Leo XIV's flight home from Spain was grounded so the king came to his aid
entries.snippet: Leo's Iberia charter, due to take him back to Rome after a weeklong visit to Spain, was grounded by a technical problem Friday, prompting Spain's king to offer his private jet instead.

entries.snippet: President Trump said Friday that a U.S. strike has killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, whom he called "the infamous leader" of the Tren de Aragua gang in Venezuela.

entries.title: Gene Shalit, longtime 'Today' show movie critic, dies at 100
entries.snippet: Known for his puffy hair, oversized handlebar mustache and a love for puns, Gene Shalit joined Today in 1970 and became arts editor in 1973. He was a middle-of-the-road critic, known for his wit and intelligence.

entries.title: Workers begin removing Trump's name from the Kennedy Center
entries.snippet: Workers began removing President Trump's name from the facade of the Kennedy Center early Saturday, hours after a court-ordered Friday deadline to remove references to Trump from the building.

entries.snippet: The Justice Department closed its investigation into the proposed $110 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers Discovery, saying it found no threat to competition or consumers.

entries.snippet: The decision paves the way for a proposed $111 billion merger uniting two rival studio giants — Paramount, owner of CBS, and the much larger Warner, which includes HBO and CNN.

entries.title: What the U.S. and Iran are demanding in the latest peace proposal
entries.snippet: The U.S. and Iran both say they are inching closer to a deal to end the war that started nearly four months ago. But as with previous announcements, there are few details on the timing and execution of any agreement. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

entries.snippet: British artist and painter David Hockney, one of the most celebrated art icons of the 20th and 21st centuries, died at the age of 88. Jeffrey Brown has a look at his life and legacy.

entries.snippet: On Sunday, an Ultimate Fighting Championship event on the White House lawn will mark both President Trump's 80th birthday and Flag Day. White House correspondent Liz Landers explains how this moment for Trump and the UFC was decades in the making.

entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including another political fight in Congress, a mixed martial arts fight at the White House and a potential deal to end fighting with Iran.

entries.snippet: Attorneys for the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk asked a judge Friday to block prosecutors from seeking the death penalty as punishment for comments they made in the media about a bullet fragment recovered from Kirk's body.

entries.title: Political blame game follows as screwworm parasite threatens cattle in Texas
entries.snippet: Screwworms are on their way to becoming a billion-dollar international problem but can be contained if ranchers are vigilant, watch their herds and other wildlife, and quickly treat any infestations, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said.

entries.snippet: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, became a symbol of middle-power resistance in January, when he declared the global rules-based order over and condemned coercion by great powers on smaller countries.

entries.title: Judge rules Trump can stage UFC fights on the White House's South Lawn this weekend
entries.snippet: A federal judge ruled on Friday that the White House is allowed to stage a UFC show this weekend in an elaborate ring already built on the South Lawn to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary — on President Donald Trump's 80th birthday.

entries.title: More than 30 lawsuits filed against aerospace company in California over damaged chemical tank
entries.snippet: More than 100 individuals — including some families with pets — as well as local businesses are suing GKN Aerospace, saying the U.K.-based company was negligent in maintaining a safe facility, especially since it's located in a large population center.

entries.title: FBI searches office of Ohio group that supports voter registration efforts
entries.snippet: Federal agents showed up at the Cleveland office of the Ohio Organizing Collaborative on Thursday and spent hours questioning staff, said Prentiss Haney, a board member of the grassroots organization.

entries.snippet: More than $60 million and tens of thousands of hours of labor have been poured into building the arena.

entries.title: As officials again say Iran war could soon end, some Trump objectives are unfulfilled

entries.title: Where Trump has lost support with independents, according to AP-NORC polling
entries.snippet: Independents have grown increasingly unhappy with President Donald Trump during his second term, a new AP-NORC polling analysis finds, particularly those without a college degree.

entries.title: Taylor Swift becomes the youngest woman inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame at age 36
entries.snippet: Taylor Swift became the youngest woman ever inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame Thursday night at age 36.

entries.title: Pope tells traffickers of migrants in the Canary Islands: Stop, repent or face God's wrath
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV warned people smugglers on Friday that they will face God's wrath for exploiting the desperation of migrants, demanding they stop and repent during his final day in this epicenter of the African migration route to Europe.

entries.title: Disaster drills helped prevent more deaths when powerful quake hit the southern Philippines
entries.snippet: Philippine officials said Friday that years of disaster-preparedness drills helped prevent a larger casualty toll when one of the strongest earthquakes in 50 years struck the south and left 46 people dead with 38 others missing.

entries.title: Germany news: Hopes high ahead of first World Cup match

entries.snippet: The firm said it was ordered to block foreign nationals from accessing its state of the art Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models on national security grounds.

entries.title: Iran war: Pakistan PM says peace deal expected in 24 hours
entries.snippet: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the US and Iran are inching closer to cementing a deal, with "finalisation likely expected in the next 24 hours."

entries.title: India news: 'Biryani date' controversy sparks debate on consent and entitlement
entries.snippet: A viral comedy show clip has triggered discussions about whether paying for a date creates expectations of intimacy, highlighting broader concerns about consent. DW has more.

entries.title: US, Venezuela say Tren de Aragua leader killed in strike
entries.snippet: The leader of the Venezuela-based Tren de Aragua gang has died in a US strike, US President Donald Trump says. The gang has been labeled a terrorist organization by Washington.

entries.title: Sudan war: UAE denies supporting RSF and Colombian recruits
entries.snippet: Human rights organizations accuse the UAE of supporting the RSF militia, which has seen a number of high-profile defections to the Sudanese Armed Forces. Meanwhile, the civilian population continues to suffer.

entries.title: Woman critically injured in shark attack at Sydney beach

entries.snippet: Paramount has been given the green light to take over Warner Bros. Discovery for $110 billion, including its subsidiary CNN, fueling fears of media censorship and increased control over the US entertainment industry.

entries.title: Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire after SpaceX IPO
entries.snippet: SpaceX floated on the Nasdaq stock exchange on Friday, with shares trading 25% above the opening price at one point. The IPO has made Musk the world's first trillionaire, at least on paper.

entries.title: World Cup: Ghana's Partey denied entry to Canada
entries.snippet: Thomas Partey, who has pleaded not guilty to several rape and sexual assault charges in the United Kingdom, has been refused a Canadian visa. He will therefore miss his team's World Cup game against Panama in Toronto.

entries.title: Iran, US say deal to end war 'has never been closer'
entries.snippet: Iran's foreign minister and the US president have both stated that an agreement to end the war in Iran could be imminent. Mediators in Pakistan say they are working "to finalize the next steps." DW has more.

entries.title: German students up in arms about funding cuts
entries.snippet: Germany's research minister, Dorothee Bär, says the situation of German students is "very privileged" and has rejected reform of the Federal Training Assistance Act (BAföG), thereby turning many students against her.

entries.title: German court holds Google liable for fake AI answers
entries.snippet: Judges in Bavaria drew a distinction between standard search engine results and AI-generated summaries. They ruled that tech giants themselves are responsible for the content of answers provided by AI.

entries.title: Iran-US deal: What are the main sticking points?

entries.title: Curacao's World Cup dream: 'Nothing is impossible'
entries.snippet: Curacao is the smallest nation ever to qualify for a World Cup. The Caribbean island is abuzz ahead of their first match on football's biggest stage – against four-time champions Germany.

entries.title: Sahel juntas are 'crushing' basic freedoms
entries.snippet: In the Sahel countries of Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, military rulers are increasingly clamping down on press freedom and freedom of expression. Many journalists, bloggers and activists have been forced into exile.

entries.title: Why is Bulgaria banning arms supplies to Ukraine?
entries.snippet: Bulgaria's new government has banned state arms supplies to Ukraine. The ban does not, however, affect commercial exports, raising the question as to whether the move was aimed more at a domestic audience than at Kyiv.

entries.title: India bets big on domestic drones for future warfare
entries.snippet: India is preparing to place its largest-ever military drone order, a procurement worth more than $2 billion that could rapidly expand the country's unmanned warfare capabilities.
